title: Binary search tree search
instructorPromptText: Write a C program that builds a Binary Search Tree (BST) from user input and implements a recursive function `int search(Node* root, int key)` that returns 1 if the key is found, and 0 otherwise.

specGateDimensions.description: Does the program define a binary tree node struct containing a value field and two child pointers (`left` and `right`)?
specGateDimensions.rationale: Binary structures require two separate child references for branching traversal.

specGateDimensions.description: Is recursive BST insertion implemented correctly, maintaining the BST property (left child <= parent < right child)?
specGateDimensions.rationale: Verifies that elements are placed such that the tree maintains sorted search properties.

specGateDimensions.description: Does the search function exploit BST properties (binary search traversal) rather than performing a full linear traversal?
specGateDimensions.rationale: A correct BST search runs in O(log N) average complexity; walking both children regardless of key value defeats the purpose of a BST.

expectedDivergences.pattern: Student traverses both left and right branches unconditionally during search, resulting in O(N) traversal.
Student inserts smaller elements on the right or larger elements on the left, violating the BST property.
Student implements the search function iteratively using a `while` loop rather than recursively.
Student hardcodes the tree values instead of building the BST dynamically from user input.
Student fails to handle a NULL root check in `search()`, causing a segmentation fault when the key is not in the tree.
